I need to write a JUnit 4 test class for DefaultKeyedValues covering all branches thoroughly, analyzing each method: getItemCount, getValue(int) with bounds checking, getKey(int) with bounds checking, getIndex(Comparable) with null and found/not-found cases, getKeys() cloning behavior, and getValue(Comparable) lookup by index.

I also need to cover addValue/setValue delegation methods, insertValue with position bounds checks and key null validation, removeValue by index or key, clear(), sortByKeys/sortByValues, equals() with all its comparison branches, hashCode(), and clone() -- while making sure supporting classes like KeyedValues, UnknownKeyException, and DefaultKeyedValue are properly exercised.

Since this is the Chart-18b module in Defects4J, the target classes are already compiled and on the classpath, so I just need to write a test class importing org.jfree.data.DefaultKeyedValues and its related types. I need to double check the correct package paths -- particularly that SortOrder comes from org.jfree.chart.util.SortOrder per the actual import statement in the source, not org.jfree.data as an older changelog entry suggested.

UnknownKeyException appears to live in org.jfree.data itself since the source throws it without any import, so I'll import it from there for the test. Now I'm laying out the full set of test methods to cover item counts, value/key lookups by index and key, index-out-of-bounds and unknown-key exception cases, adding and setting values (including null key/value handling), and insertion behavior including out-of-bounds positions and null keys.

I continue listing tests for insertion at existing positions and moving keys, removal by index and key with rebuild behavior, clearing, sorting by keys and values (ascending, descending, and with nulls sorting to the end per documentation), and the equals/hashCode/clone contract covering same-instance, type mismatches, differing counts, differing keys, null value combinations, and equal instances. For the null-sort test, I'll rely on the documented behavior that null values sort to the end regardless of order, trusting the underlying comparator implementation.

I also note the removal-by-index branch skips the rebuild when removing the last element since the index equals the size after removal — I need to think about whether this has any externally testable effect given the index map is private.

I'll write the test asserting getIndex("C") equals -1 after removal, following the documented contract, which should expose the fault if the implementation returns a stale index instead.

I also want to test removeValue on a middle index to trigger a rebuild, then verify getIndex still works for remaining items, and cover the insertValue branch where pos equals position, which happens when a key is already present at that exact spot.

I should also cover the else branch where pos differs from position, moving an existing key to a new insertion point by removing the old entry and re-adding it, plus the case where pos is negative and the key isn't found so it simply inserts without removal. Writing the full test code now, along with a check for addValue with a null value.

Now for equals(): I need to verify it returns false when keys don't match, and test the "different class" branch using an object that isn't a KeyedValues instance to confirm equals returns false. Writing final test code with proper imports and structure...

I'll place the test class in the same package as the source, so no import statement is needed for the target class itself, naming the class DefaultKeyedValuesTest as required.

Actually, I'll skip the package declaration entirely and import the target classes directly, since default package files can still work as long as the classes are public. I'll finalize the complete test suite along with the summary table.
